clue.text: Hide onset of chronic pain

indicators.note: the onset of something is its beginning, so only the opening letter of the next word is kept

parts.note: the first letter of chronic
an ache is a dull pain

explanation.surface: A patient conceals the first signs of a long-term pain.
explanation.definitionFit: To cache something is to stow it in a secret store, a synonym for concealing it.

clue.text: Investigate possibility of ripping off patient

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to ... a place is to reconnoitre it before robbing it

explanation.surface: Someone looks into whether a patient might be exploited.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Patient' reads as an adjective or as the victim of the rip-off; it is a separate noun meaning. To 'case the joint' is criminal slang for scouting before a burglary.
explanation.definitionFit: Case is thieves' slang for scouting a target, and a medical case is a person under treatment.

clue.text: Awful cameraman who could be better

parts.note: crap is slang for very bad
a cameraman shoots film, so is a shooter

explanation.surface: A poor cameraman who could do a better job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Better' looks like the comparative of good, but here it means one who bets. The whole definition is a person, matching the gambler at the dice table.
explanation.definitionFit: A crapshooter plays the dice game craps, staking money on throws, so is literally someone who bets.

clue.text: Catch business associate coming back after finishing early

indicators.note: coming back means travelling the other way, so the word is read from end to start
a word that finishes early stops before its last letter, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: a partner in a firm is a business associate

explanation.surface: A colleague returns after leaving work early and is caught out.
explanation.walkthrough: PARTNER loses its R to give PARTNE, which reversed is ENTRAP.
explanation.definitionFit: To entrap someone is to snare or trick them, a synonym for catch.

clue.text: Fetching new red coat for Idris Elba

indicators.note: a new version of something has been remade, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: a coat is the outer layer, so only the outside letters of the name are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of Idris
taken as written

explanation.surface: A wardrobe department gives the actor Idris Elba an attractive new red coat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fetching' looks like going to get the coat; it is the adjective meaning attractive.
explanation.definitionFit: Fetching means attractive or appealing, which is what desirable describes.

clue.text: Misled into supporting dreadful Conservative Government

indicators.note: something misled is sent the wrong way, so the following letters go astray into a new order
in a down entry, a piece supporting another sits underneath it, so it comes last

parts.note: dire means dreadful
C is the standard abbreviation for Conservative
the letters of into, rearranged

explanation.surface: Voters are fooled into backing an awful Tory administration.
explanation.definitionFit: Direction is the act of managing or controlling, an older sense of government as guidance.

clue.text: Ship's primary means of propulsion using blades?

definitions.text: Ship's primary means of propulsion using blades?

indicators.note: the primary letter of a word is its first, so just the start of the word is used

parts.note: the first letter of ship
a rowing crew drives a boat with the blades of their oars

explanation.surface: A question about how a vessel is mainly driven through the water.
explanation.walkthrough: Read whole, the clue also describes the answer: a ship's propeller drives it with rotating blades.
explanation.definitionFit: A screw is the bladed propeller at a ship's stern, its main source of thrust.

clue.text: Scrupulous doctor able to absorb material without pressure

parts.note: to doctor results is to rig them

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the following item is taken out of the word before it

parts.note: a porous substance soaks things up
P is the symbol for pressure

explanation.surface: A careful physician who can soak up fabric without any stress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like the person in the surface; it is the verb meaning to falsify.
explanation.definitionFit: Rigorous means thorough and exacting, which is what a scrupulous person is.

clue.text: Boring item input to computer had an effect

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a drill's cutting piece, and also a binary digit fed to a computer
second meaning: past tense of a verb used of a measure that starts to take hold

explanation.surface: Some dull data entry nonetheless made a difference.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boring' looks like dull; it is drilling, and a drill's tip is a bit, as is the smallest unit of computer data.
explanation.definitionFit: When a policy bites it takes effect, so its past tense describes something that had an impact.

clue.text: Pretend computer systems issue involves accuracy

indicators.note: something that involves other things wraps them up inside itself

parts.note: to exude is to issue or ooze out
to act is to pretend
IT is information technology

explanation.surface: A sham computer problem is all about precision.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Issue' looks like a problem with the systems; here it is the verb meaning to seep out, and it is the outer piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Exactitude is the quality of being exact, a synonym for precision and accuracy.

clue.text: Broadcast The Jazz Singer?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to throw seed widely
second meaning: a jazz singer who scats, singing nonsense syllables

explanation.walkthrough: The Jazz Singer is the famous 1927 talkie, so 'broadcast' seems to be about airing it; the question mark flags a whimsical noun for one who scats.
explanation.definitionFit: To scatter seed is to broadcast it by hand, and a scatter is jokingly someone who scat-sings.

clue.text: Sporting event blasted target area

indicators.note: something blasted is blown apart, so the letters are scattered and reassembled

parts.note: taken as written
A is the abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: A shooting contest where the target zone was blown up.
explanation.definitionFit: A regatta is a meeting of boat races, a sporting occasion on the water.

clue.text: School checks faculty have good reasons for rifle permit?

indicators.note: to check something is to hold it in, so one word is held inside the other

parts.note: SCH is an abbreviation of school
hearing is one of the faculties, and the ear is its organ
to warrant something is to justify it

explanation.surface: A school department justifies its need for a gun licence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rifle' looks like a gun, but it is the verb meaning to ransack; the question mark flags the twist.
explanation.definitionFit: A search warrant is a legal document authorising police to go through, or rifle, a property.

clue.text: What damages growth is seniority surprisingly, not diversity

indicators.note: turning out surprisingly means coming out in an unexpected form, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: age brings seniority
the letters of not, rearranged
a range is a diversity or variety

explanation.surface: A puzzling remark about what holds back a career: seniority rather than diversity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Growth' suggests career progress; it means vegetation.
explanation.definitionFit: Agent Orange was the herbicide sprayed by US forces in Vietnam to strip foliage, so it destroys plant life.

clue.text: Fortunate adult wary, not having succeeded initially

parts.note: A is the film-rating abbreviation for adult

indicators.note: not having something means lacking it, so that item is removed from the word
initially points at the earliest occurrence, so it is the first copy of the letter that goes

parts.note: suspicious means wary
S is the abbreviation for succeeded, as in family trees

explanation.surface: A grown-up who was cautious at first and failed got lucky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Initially' says which S goes: the first one in SUSPICIOUS, leaving A + USPICIOUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Auspicious means favourable or promising good luck, close to fortunate.

clue.text: Well acquainted with and in contact with

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to be ... a subject is to know it well
second meaning: on top of, touching a surface

explanation.walkthrough: Read as two words, 'up on' means well informed; as one word it is the preposition meaning on.
explanation.definitionFit: Being up on news means knowing it, and the preposition upon means resting on or touching something.

clue.text: Fresh nurses start to re-examine rash

indicators.note: to nurse something is to hold it close, so one piece is cradled inside another

parts.note: fresh can mean cheeky or impudent

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter, so only that letter is used

parts.note: the first letter of the hyphenated word

explanation.surface: A new skin rash prompts a second look by the doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fresh' and 'rash' look medical; fresh means cheeky and rash is the adjective meaning hasty.
explanation.definitionFit: Imprudent means unwise and reckless, a synonym of rash used as an adjective.

clue.text: Gunpowder in small batches?

parts.note: surface reading: explosive measured out in little portions
setter's reading: a gun is a piece and powder is meal, so the compound word itself means bit by bit

explanation.surface: Explosives handed out a little at a time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gunpowder' looks like one word to be defined, but it splits into gun and powder; the question mark flags that.
explanation.definitionFit: Piecemeal means done bit by bit, a little at a time rather than all at once.

clue.text: Stupid advice to overworked crossword compiler?

definitions.meaning: second meaning: read as two words, a suggestion to write fewer of something a setter produces

explanation.surface: Telling an exhausted setter to cut back is a dim idea.
explanation.definitionFit: Clueless is informal for ignorant or dim, and split in two it urges a setter to write fewer clues.

clue.text: Criticise church taking instrument back in fit of pique

indicators.note: taking something in means holding it inside, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: to pan a show is to criticise it harshly

indicators.note: back means going in the opposite direction, so the instrument is spelt from its end

parts.note: a lute is a stringed instrument
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Someone attacks a church for bringing back an instrument, in a temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fit of pique' sits at the end looking like part of the story; it is the definition, while 'church' comes last in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Petulance is sulky bad temper, the state shown in a fit of pique.

clue.text: Sexually attractive male boss

definitions.meaning: first meaning: slang for a virile, attractive man
second meaning: a raised knob or ornamental ... on a surface

explanation.walkthrough: 'Boss' seems to be a manager; it is the ornamental knob sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A stud is slang for a sexy man and also a projecting metal knob, which is what a boss is.

clue.text: Cover opening of store in advance of publicity?

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter, so only that is taken

parts.note: the first letter of store
pre- means before
an ad is a piece of publicity

explanation.surface: Press coverage of a shop launch ahead of its marketing push.
explanation.definitionFit: To spread a cloth over a table is to cover it, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Cleaner ticks off mourner

parts.note: to carpet someone is to reprimand them
a weeper is someone who cries, such as a mourner

explanation.surface: A cleaning lady scolds a grieving person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cleaner' looks like a person; it is the hand-pushed device with rotating brushes.
explanation.definitionFit: A carpet-sweeper is a manual appliance with brushes for picking up dirt from rugs, a household cleaning tool.

clue.text: Flesh out support provided by board

indicators.note: out can mean disordered or wrong, so the letters are put into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A management board backs a plan with fuller detail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flesh out' reads as a phrasal verb meaning to add detail; it splits into fodder and signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A shelf is a flat board fixed to a wall that holds things up, so it is a support made of board.

clue.text: Saint guided Bob?

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for saint
to lead is to guide

explanation.surface: Was a holy man's guide named Bob?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bob' looks like a man's name; it is a bobsleigh, and the question mark marks the definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: A bob, or bobsleigh, is a kind of racing sled used on ice runs.

clue.text: Indecent milieu and activities of former pupils?

parts.note: OB stands for old boy, a former pupil of a school
a scene is a social setting and the goings-on in it

explanation.surface: A school reunion's crowd and goings-on turned rude.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay reads as the old boys' scene: OB + SCENE. Old boy is British usage for a former pupil of a particular school.
explanation.definitionFit: Obscene means offensive to accepted standards of decency, a stronger synonym of indecent.

clue.text: Gentleman incarcerated in prison following revolution

indicators.note: a revolution turns things round, so the captured letters are read from right to left
something incarcerated is locked inside, so the letters are tucked within the next word

parts.note: the middle letters of prison

explanation.surface: A gentleman is jailed after an uprising.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir is the polite form of address for a man, and the title of a knight.

clue.text: Unchanging exterior masking sign of affection

indicators.note: to mask something is to hide it from view, so that symbol vanishes from the word

parts.note: external means on the outside
X is a kiss at the end of a letter

explanation.surface: A poker-faced outer manner hiding real tenderness.
explanation.definitionFit: Eternal means lasting for ever and never altering, a near synonym for unchanging.

clue.text: Son flusters about causing tension

indicators.note: about can mean round in a different way, so the letters are turned into a fresh order

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son
taken as written

explanation.surface: A boy gets his parents in a state, making things tense.
explanation.definitionFit: Stressful describes something that produces anxiety and strain, which is to cause tension.

clue.text: Fear about to transfix old man

indicators.note: to transfix is to pierce right through, so one piece is driven into the middle of another

parts.note: old man is slang for father
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Anxiety about to paralyse an elderly father.
explanation.definitionFit: Dread is deep apprehension, a synonym for fear as a noun.
